title: Sell Mineral Rights in Farmington, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Farmington, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Farmington, Fayette County? We buy oil, gas, and royalty interests around the Route 40 and Chalk Hill area. No pressure to sell.
heroLead: Farmington sits along the old National Road near Fort Necessity, and the same ridge-and-valley land that George Washington once fought over has been leased and re-leased for gas rights for decades.
intro: Farmington is a Fayette County community along Route 40, close enough to Fort Necessity National Battlefield that most locals grew up hearing about the history before they ever thought about what's under their own land. That land, spread across the ridges toward Chalk Hill and the Summit Mountain area, carries oil and gas potential that's been leased in waves since well before Marcellus.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Farmington, whether you're holding a producing interest, an older lease that's gone quiet, or a fractional share from family land.

sections.heading: Ridge country on the edge of the play
paragraphs: The terrain around Farmington is steep and ridge-heavy compared to the flatter farmland further north in the county, which has historically made large-scale horizontal development here more limited. That doesn't mean no activity — it means development is more selective about where units get placed.

sections.heading: Old leases in a tourism-adjacent area
paragraphs: Because this area draws visitors for Fort Necessity and the nearby ski resorts, some landowners assume their property is off-limits to drilling. That's not automatically true — surface use restrictions and mineral rights are separate questions, and we look at the actual lease and deed language rather than assumptions.

sections.heading: What we need to give you a real number
paragraphs: Send whatever documents you have — lease, deed, royalty statement — and we'll review lease terms, producing status, and nearby activity before naming a figure.

faqs.question: Does being near Fort Necessity affect whether I can sell my mineral rights near Farmington?
faqs.answer: No, being near a historic site doesn't itself restrict mineral rights ownership or sale. Any surface use restrictions would come from specific easements or agreements, which we'd review as part of the title work.

faqs.question: Is Farmington's terrain a problem for gas development?
faqs.answer: The ridge terrain here has historically made large horizontal units less common than in flatter parts of Fayette County, but it doesn't eliminate value — it just makes tract-specific review more important.

faqs.question: I have an old lease from decades ago near Farmington. Is it still active?
faqs.answer: It depends on the lease's held-by-production and renewal terms. We review the actual document to determine whether it's still in effect before discussing a purchase.
